Clause 1.   This Regulation is called the “Chulalongkorn Univers ity Regulation on Undergraduate
Clause 2.   This Regulation shall be applicable for students who commence their stud ies

Clause 3.   The following s shall be repealed:

This Regulation supersedes any prior Regulations, Rules, Announcements, Orders, Resolutions, or

Clause 4.   In this Regulation:
“University” means Chulalong korn University
“Faculty” encompasses schools, colleges, and divisions under other designations of equivalent

“Dea n” means the d ean of the faculties, schools, and colleges within which the program is

“ The A dministrative Board of the Faculty ” encompasses the administrative board of schools,

“ The Administrative Board of the Program ” means the administrative board of programs with in the

“Head of Department” means the head of the department within which the program is affiliated

“Special Lecturer” means a course instructor who is not a full - time lecturer.

University Council and of which the Board of the Higher Education Commission has   been notifie d for

“Student” means a student of Chulalongkorn University , both full - time and part - time.
Clause 5.   Students shall comply with relevant Regulations, Rules, Announcements, Orders, or
other Guidelines, as stipulated by the university or the division, provided they do not conflict with provisions under
this Regulation.
Clause 6.   The University President shall have charge and control over the execution of this
Regulation and shall have power to issue Rules , Announcements, Orders, Directives, or Criteria for the execution of
this Regulation.
In case where interpretation issues or problems arise under this Regulation, the University President
is entrusted with final deliberating and issuing Order s as considered expedient .
Chapter 1
General Provision
Clause 7.   All u niversi ty staff and special lecturers engaged in the execution of undergraduate
programs in accordance with this Regulation shall possess the requisite requirements prescribed by the prevailing
university r ules and r egulation s and as determined by the Board of Ac ademic Policy .
Chapter 2
Education Management
Section 1
Academic System
Clause 8.   The undergraduate studies shall be governed by credit - based systems encompassing
semester, trimester, module, or other systems as determined by the University Council.
Clause 9.   The aca demic system shall be as follows :
(1)   The s emester system means the academic system that divides an academic year into 2
semesters , which are the first semester and the second semester, with an optional inclusion of the summer semester
following the second sem ester.
(2)   The trimester system means the academic system that divides an academic year into 3
semesters , which are the first semester, the second semester , and the third semester.
(3)   The module system means the academic system that divides an academic year into more than
3 sub - semesters , as determined by the program.
(4)   Other academic system s as determined by the program.
In the case of the semester system, each   shall encompass a study duration of not less
than 15 weeks, whereas the summer semester shall en compass a study duration of approximately 6 weeks , provided
the total cumulative teaching hours of each course remain commensurate with the teaching hours allocated for a
semester .
In the case of the trimester system, each   shall encompass a study duration of not less
than 12 weeks, provided 1 trimester - based credit is equivalent to 12/15 semester - based credit, or 5 trimester - based
credits is equivalent to 4 semester - based credits.
In the case of the module and other systems, details of the academi c system, criteria governing
credit calculation, and details for translating credits to semester - based equivalents shall be explicitly outlined in the
official documentation of the program .
Clause 10.   A unit denoting the amount of academic study is called a “credit . ” The assignment of
credits for each course is subject to the following criteria:
(1)   A theory - based course, comprising 1 hour of lecture or discussion per week for the duration of
the semester or approximately 15 hours in the semester , is assigned 1 semester - based credit. In the case of online
pedagogy , the duration of 1.5 hours is equivalent to 0.1 semester - based credit.
(2)   A laboratory - based course, comprising 2 to 3 hours of practice or experiment per week for the
duration of the   or approximately 30 t o 45 hours in the   , is assigned 1 semester -   In the
case of online laboratory sessions, experiments, or practices, a duration of 3 hours is equivalent to 0.1 semester -
based credit.
(3)   A training or fieldwork (professional internships), com prising 3 to 6 hours per week for the
duration of the   or approximately 45 to 90 hours in the   , is assigned 1 semester -
(4)   A project or other course - related activit ies , comprising at least 45 hours of work for the
duration of the   , is assigned 1 semester - based credit.
Other criteria or methods for apportioning instructional and recess durations within 1 hour shall be
in accordance with relevant university announcement s .
Clause 11.   A course listed in the O fficial D ocumentation of the P rogram, requiring students to
obtain a designation of S but not factoring into the total credits required for program completion , shall be
designated as a “non - credit course.”
Students , who obtain a grade of U in the course under paragraph one, are require d to re - register in
the said course.
Clause 12.   The calculation of students’ register ed credits is designated as follows:
(1)   “ Credit Attempted : CA ” means the total number of credits from all courses , graded with A, B+,
B, C+, C, D+, D , and F , which the student has regis tered in each semester.
(2)   “ Cumulative Credit Attempted : CAX ” means the cumulative number of credits from all
courses, graded with A, B+, B, C+, C, D+, D , and F , which the student has registered in all semesters, and includes all
courses that the student regi sters more than one occasion .
(3)   “ Credit Granted : CG ” means the total number of credits which the student has obtained a
grade of A, B+, B, C+, C, D+, D , and S in each semester.
(4)   “ Cumulative Credit Granted : CGX ” means the cumulative number of credits from all courses
which the student has obtained a grade of A, B+, B, C+, C, D+, D , and S. In case where a student has successfully
completed a course on multiple occasions or has passed a course deemed equivalent to one previously passed,
only the credits from the first successful attempt will be counted.
Section 2
Period of Study
Clause 13.   A “Period of Study” means a duration that students undertake to complete the
studies as determined by the program.
The period of study under paragraph one shall commence from the inaug ural semester of the
student's primary enrollment into the program and conclude in the semester wherein the student successfully
passes all requisite examinations and fulfil l s all criteria as determined by the program.
Clause 14.   Individuals enrolled in a full - time undergraduate program shall have their period of
study determined based on the following criteria:
(1)   Not exceeding 8 academic years for a 4 - year program
(2)   Not exceeding 10 academic years for a 5 - year program
(3)   Not exceeding 12 academic years for a 6 - year program
Clause 15.   The period of study for a part - time undergraduate program shall be in accordance with
the relevant university regulations.
Section 3
Language of Instruction
Clause 16.   The language of instruction for undergraduate programs may be delivered in either
Thai or a for eign language, but such information shall be duly communicated to prospective candidates preceding
their formal application submission.
During the study, a course instructor may deliver instruction in either Thai or a foreign language.
Upon entering the p rogram , the language of instruction for each respective course shall be duly
communicated to the students before the course registration for that academic year.
Chapter 3
Admissions
Clause 17.   Applicants to undergraduate program s must possess a Secondary Education or an
equivalent qualification accredited by the Ministry of Education, in addition to fulfilling other prerequisites as
determined by the respective program.
Clause 18.   Admission procedures may encompass written examinations, selection, or other
methods as determin ed by the Administrative Board of the Faculty , subject to approval by the Board of Academic
Affairs.
Chapter 4
Registration
Section 1
Initial Enrol l ment
Clause 19.   Individuals who have been admitted and conferred student status by the university
shall complet e their initial enrollment by furnishing requisite documents and corroborative evidence in accordance
with the Guideline s and within the timeframe as determined by the Office of the Registrar , as well as register ing for
their respective courses and remit t i ng tuition along with any other pertinent fees .
Section 2
Course Registration
Clause 20.   Course registration in the semester or trimester system is divided into 2 classifications :
(1)   Regular registration can be executed bef ore the commencement of each semester .
(2)   Late registration can be executed within the first 2 weeks of the semester or within the first
week of the summer semester and is subject to a fine as stipulated by the university announcement .
The details regarding the date, time, and procedure for both classifications of registration shall be
determined by the Office of the Registrar.
Course registration under the module or other system shall be in accordance with the
Announcement from the Office of the Registrar.
Clause 21.   S tudents are permitted to register for courses in the semester or trimester system up
to a maximum of 22 semester - based credits for each semester and up to 9 semester - based credits for the summer
semester .
Credits attributed to courses registered in the m odule or other systems shall be calculated in
proportion to the number of credits specified under paragraph one .
Clause 22.   C ourse registration beyond the stipulated courses of the enrolled program , where a
student opts not to be graded in a hierarchical manner, can be executed within the course addition period as
outlined in Clause 28 by submitting a forma l request to the Office of the Registrar , accompanied by the
endorsement of the advisor and the approval of the course instructor. The total number of credits, incl usive of these
courses, shall not exceed the threshold specified in Clause 21.
Clause 23.   Course registration as a visit or student shall be in accordance with Clause 22.
Clause 24.   Course registration requires the endorsement of the advisor and shall be in accordance
with the d irectives as determined by the respective program.
Section 3
Course Exemption
Clause 25.   Students may be granted exemption from certain courses within the program of study,
provided they have previously undertaken and successfully passed an undergraduate - level cou rse at Chulalongkorn
University, the content of which is equivalent to that of the course from which exemption is sought, and wherein the
student has obtaine d a grade of S or not less than C .
The course from which an exemption is sought under paragraph one must have been completed
within the 5 academic years immediately preceding the semester in which the course exemption is being sought.
Applications for course exemption shall be submitted within the first semester of initial enrol l ment
and shall require the endorsement of the Administrative Board of the Program and the approval of the
Administrative Board of the Faculty .
The Administrative Board of the Program may specify additional criteria for course exemption.
Clause 26.   In the case where a course exemption has b een granted, and the student has
subsequently studied and passed the non - exempted courses within their program, it shall be deemed that the
student has successfully completed all courses in accordance with the total number of credits stipulated for that
pr ogram.
Clause 27.   Grades obtained from the exempted courses shall not be factor ed into the calculation
of the program's Grade Point Average (GPA). The duration of study shall be adjusted in proportion to the number of
exempted credits relative to the total credits re quired for the program and shall be considered an integral part of
the total period of study.
Students who are granted a course exemption shall be ineligible to receive the award medal as
stipulated under Clause 73.
Section 4
Course Addition, Dropping, a nd Withdrawal
Clause 28.   Course addition in the semester or trimester system can be executed within the first 2
weeks of the semester or within the first week of the summer semester.
Course addition under the module or other system shall be in accordance with the An nouncement
from the Office of the Registrar.
Clause 29.   Course dropping in the semester or trimester system can be executed within the first 6
weeks of the semester or within the first 2 weeks of the summer semester, with the dropped courses not being
recorded o n th e academic transcript.
Course dropping under the module or other system shall be in accordance with the Announcement
from the Office of the Registrar.
Clause 30.   Course withdrawal in the semester or trimester system can be executed after the first
6 weeks but not bey ond t he 12th week of the semester or after the first 2 weeks but not beyond the 4th week of
the summer semester, with the withdrawn courses being recorded o n the academic transcript.
In case of course withdrawal after the 12th week of the semester or after the 4th week of the
summer semester, a penalty fee, as stipulated by the university announcement , shall be settled within the 15th
week of the semester or within the 5th week of the summer semester. The settlement shall be executed at a
minimum of 3 worki ng days before the examination date of that course.
Course withdrawal under the module or other system shall be in accordance with the
Announcement from the Office of the Registrar.
Clause 31.   Course addition and dropping require the endorsement of the advisor, wher eas course
withdrawal requires the approval of the Dean as per the endorsement of the advisor and the course instructor .
Clause 32.   In semesters other than the summer semester, after course dropping and withdrawal,
students shall remain registered at a minimum of 1 c ourse .
Section 5
Course Re - registration
Clause 33.   Course re - registration is subject to the following criteria:
(1)   Students who obtain a grade of F U or W f rom a compulsory course are required to re - register
for that course until they obtain a grade of A B+ B C+ C D+ D or S.
(2)   Students who obtain a grade of F U or W fr om an elective course may re - register for that
course or opt for an alternative course.
(3)   In addition to cases under (1) and (2), students may re - register for any courses, and such
registration under this pr ovision is called “Focused Study”.
(4)   All g rades obtained from courses under re - registration or focused study shall be recorded o n
the academic transcript.
Section 6
Course Attendance
Clause 34.   Students shall meet the minimum attendance requirements for courses in wh ich they
are registered as stipulated by the university or the division.
Chapter 5
Assessment
Section 1
Grading Designation
Clause 35.   Grading for each course shall be executed with the following designations, each of
which carries specific meanings and weigh ts as outlined below.
Designation   Meaning   Weight
A   Excellent   4.0
B+   Very Good   3.5
B   Good   3.0
C+   Fairly Good   2.5
C   Fair   2.0
D+   Poor   1.5
D   Very Poor   1.0
F   Fail   0.0
I   Incomplete   -
M   Missing   -
P   In progress   -
S   Satisfactory   -
U   Unsatisfactory   -
V   Visitor   -
W   Withdrawn   -
X   No report   -
Section 2
Grading Criteria
Clause 36.   Grading shall be executed at the completion of study in each semester .
Clause 37.   Grading using the designations A B+ B C+ C D+ D or F shall be executed based on the
following criteria:
(1)   For course s wherein students take examinations and/or produce works subject to hierarchical
grading.
(2)   T ransition from the designation I , provided the final grade h as been submitted to the Office of
the Registrar before the conclusion of the first 2 weeks of the subse quent semester in which the student is
registered. In the case of Clauses 39(1) and 39(2), the final grade may be considered not to exceed a grade of C, in
accordance with the criteria as stipulated by the university announcement .
(3)   T ransition from the desig nations M P or X.
Clause 38.   Grading using the designation F, in addition to Clause 37, shall be executed based on
the following criteria:
(1)   For courses wherein students are not permitted to take examination s .
(2)   In case of academic misconduct wherein students are awarde d a grade of F in accordance with
Clause 60.
(3)   T ransition from the designation I after the conclusion of the first 2 weeks of the subsequent
semester in which the student is registered.
(4)   T ransition from the designation M after the conclusion of the first 2 we eks of the subsequent
semester .
Clause 39.   Grading using the designation I shall be executed based on the following criteria:
(1)   S tudents fall ill before an examination, leading to an inability to take some or all course
examinations, provided they comply with the proce dures under Clause 53 , and t he Dea n , accompanied by the
endorsement of the course instructor, may grant approval following the view that the contents of student's studies
are only marginally incomplete.
(2)   Students fall ill during the course examinations , lea ding to an inability to take some or all
course examinations, provided they comply with the procedures under Clause 53 and obtain approval from the
Dean.
(3)   Students fail to appear for a course examination due to force majeure, and the Administrative
Board o f the Faculty with which the students are affiliated grants approval in accordance with the criteria set forth by
the university announcement .
(4)   S tudents are unable to complete work constituting a portion of the course requirements , and
the course instructor considers it expedient to postpone the grading, provided such a decision must be supported by
the endorsement of the Head of the Department (if applicable). The course instructor shall then provide written
notification to the Office of the Registrar along with the submission of grades of other students registered in that
course.
Clause 40.   Grading using the designation M shall be executed for courses in which students fail to
appear for the course examination and remain unable to furnish complete evidence justifying such absence.
Clause 41.   Grading using the designation P shall be executed at the conclusion of teaching or
Clause 42.   Grading using the designation S shall be executed upon the ass essment being dee med
satisfactory in the following courses:
(1)   For courses which the program specifies to be graded in a non - hierarchical manner .
(2)   For courses in which students register in accordance with Clause 22.
Clause 43.   Grading using the designation U shall be executed for course s outlined in Clause 42 ,
but the assessment is deemed unsatisfactory.
Clause 44.   Grading using the designation V shall be executed for courses wherein students are
granted approval to register as visitor students in accordance with Clause 23, contingent upon meeting the
attendance requirements set forth by the university, the division, or the course instructor, accompanied by the
course instructor’s decision that the students have demonstrated diligence throughout the course.
Clause 45.   In addition to cases of academic misconduc t under Clause 60, Clause 61, or Clause 62,
grading using the designation W in the semester or trimester system shall be executed after the first 6 weeks of the
semester or after the first 2 weeks of the summer semester in the following circumstances:
(1)   Stu dents are granted course withdrawal in accordance with Clause 30.
(2)   S tudents fall ill before an examination, leading to an inability to take some or all course
examinations , provided they comply with the procedures under Clause 53, and the Dean and the cours e instructor
concur th at a significant portion of the content of student’s studies remains incomplete and consider expedient to
withdraw the course.
(3)   Students take a leave of absence in accordance with the grounds set forth in Clause 54 or
Clause 55.
(4)   Studen ts are ordered to take a leave of absence in accordance with grounds not encompassed
within Clause 60, Clause 61, or Clause 62.
(5)   The Dean approves the transition from the designation I that is given under Clause 39(1),
Clause 39(2), or Clause 39(3) due to t he unresolved illness or force majeure.
(6)   For courses wherein students are granted approval to register as visitor students in accordance
with Clause 23 but fail to meet the attendance requirements set forth by the university, the division, or the course
in structor, or the course instructor decides that the students have not demonstrated diligence throughout the
course .
(7)   For courses wherein students have registered contrary to the prescribed registration conditions.
Grading using the designation W in the modu le or other system shall be in accordance with the
Announcement from the Office of the Registrar.
Section 3
Calculation of Grade Point Average
Clause 46.   The c alculati on of the Grade Point Average of each student shall be executed at the
completion of each semester .
Clause 47.   Grade Point Average is divided into 2 classifications:
(1)   The Semester Grade Point Average shall be calculated based on the student's grades for each
semester by summing the assigned credits and the weight of each designation the student receives for each c ourse
and subsequently dividing the sum by the total number of Credit Attempted (CA) .
(2)   The Cumulative Grade Point Average shall be calculated based on the student’s grades from
the semester of initial enrollment until the semester of calculation by summing the assigned credits and the weight
of each designation the student receives for each course and subsequently dividing the sum by the total number of
Cumulative Credit Attempted (CA X ) .
Section 4
Classification of Student Status
Clause 48.   Student status is divided into 2 classifications: regular status and probationary status.
(1)   Regular status students are as follows:
(a)   Students who enroll in the inaugural semester , or
(b)   Students who obtain a Cumulative Grade Point Average of not less than 2.00.
(2)   Probationary status stude nts are students who obtain a Cumulative Grade Point Average from
Clause 49.   For the classification of student status, it shall be determined whether the student
holds a regular or probationary status in accordance with Clause 48.
Clause 50.   The classification of student status shall be determined at the completion of the
semester wherein the academic assessment occurs or at the completion of the final summer semester for students
who have fulfilled all program requirements and have obtained all necessary qualifica tions before graduation. For
students in their inaugural semester , the classification of student status will be determined at the completion of
their second   as from the initial enrollment.
Clause 51.   The grades from the summer semester shall be combined with the grades of the
subsequent   in which students are registered and with calculable credits for the purpose of the
classif ication of student status.
Chapter 6
Sick Leave
Clause 52.   Sick leave is divided into 2 classifications:
(1)   “Sick leave before examination ” means students fall ill before the teaching of the semester or
summer semester is completed , and the illness continues to persist up to and including the date of the examination ,
leading to an inability to take some or all course examinations .
(2)   “Sick leav e during an examination” means students who have completed all studies until the
completion of the semester or the summer semester but fall ill, leading to an inability to take some or all course
examinations .
Clause 53.   For sick leave in accordance with Clause 52, s tudents must submit a formal request to
the Dean for approval within 1 week from the date when the student first became ill , accompanied by a medical
certificate obtained from the Chulalongkorn University Health Centre, Office of Student Affairs, a governm ental
health institution, or a private health institution accredited by the Ministry of Public Health.
Chapter 7
Leave of Absence
Clause 54.   Within the last teaching date of the semester as stipulated in the academic calendar ,
and before the examination date of, or in case of no assessment, the course in which the student is registered ,
students may submit a formal request to the Dean for the approval of a leave of absence under the following
conditions:
(1)   Subjected to mandatory conscription or summoned for military d uties.
(2)   Receiving an international exchange student scholarship or other scholarship s with direct
educational benefit to the student ’s higher education study .
(3)   Suffering from an illness requiring hospitali z ation for a duration extending beyond   3
consecutive weeks.
(4)   Suffering from an illness mandating a recovery period of 3 consecutive weeks as prescribed by
a medical professional.
(5)   Encountering personal exigencies , with the endorsement from the Administrative Board of the
Faculty.
A leave of absence under (3) a nd (4) must be accompanied by a medical certificate in accordance
with Clause 53 .
Clause 55.   In case of force majeure necessitating a leave of absence for reasons not covered
under Clause 54, students must submit at the earliest opportunity a formal request to the De an , and the
Administrative Board of the Faculty in which the student is affiliated shall determine the approval in accordance with
criteria as stipulated in the university announcement .
Clause 56.   A leave of absence under Clause 54 and Clause 55 may be granted on a per -
submission basis, with each grant not exceeding the duration of 2 semesters . Should the necessity for additional
leave of absence persist, students must submit a new formal request .
Clause 57.   In case a leave of absence is approved , t he duration of the leave will be inclusive
within the period of study , except when such leave is granted under Clause 54(1) or on other grounds as determined
by the university.
Clause 58.   During a leave of absence, students are obliged to pay the status maintenance fee to
maintain their student status for each semester in accordance with the university announcement unless the tuition
fee for that semester has been previously settled . Otherwise, t he student status shall be terminated .
During a leave of absence, the Office of the Registrar shall ci rculate the notification to the division to
suspend all university or faculty services except healthcare - related student services.
Clause 59.   Upon the return to study following the leave of absence , the student status will revert
to its prior state preceding the lea ve of absence.
Chapter 8
Academic Misconduct
Clause 60.   In case a student is found to have committed academic misconduct or contribute d to
such misconduct during the course examination of each semester , the mid - term course examination, or the course
examination d ur ing a semester as administered by the faculty or the course instructor to assess the learning
outcome, the Dean of the faculty with which the student is affiliated shall consider implementing the followings:
(1)   In case of cheating , depending on the circumsta nces and severity of the conduct, the following
may be implemented:
(a)   Termination of student status .
(b)   Awarding of the designation F or U, as applicable, for the course wherein the cheating
occurred , withdrawal from all other courses registered in the semeste r of the misconduct , and a deduction of 20
behavio ral points.
(2)   In case of a likelihood of cheating, the course wherein the likelihood occurs shall be a warded a
designation F and a deduction of 15 behavioral points.
(3)   For other misconduct as stipulated in rele vant R egulations, R ules, A nnouncements, D irectives,
or O rders regarding examination, appropriate measures shall be implemented proportional to the misconduct but
shall not exceed the assignment of designation F for the course wherein misconduct occurred an d/or a deduction of
10 behavioral points.
For the implementation under paragraph one, the Dean shall appoint a fact - finding committee
chaired by a designated vice dean, with additional members not exceeding 5 individuals . The committee is endowed
with the authority to collect evidence, summon individuals for testimony or statements, and submit findings to the
Dean for the implementation of appropriate measures under paragraph on e, followed by reporting to the
Administrative Board of the Faculty for acknowle dgment . All procedures shall be completed without delay .
The fact - finding procedure under paragraph two must ensure that the student, who is alleged to
have committed or contributed to the misconduct, is duly informed of the facts and afforded the opportu nity to
contest and present their own evidence, as well as being informed of their rights in accordance with administrative
procedure law, which includes: the right to challenge a committee member for potential direct or indirect conflicts
of interest in t he case under consideration; the right to inspect document s necessary for making an objection,
providing an explanation, or safeguarding their rights; and t he right to be accompanied by legal counsel or an advisor
during the explanation before the committe e.
Clause 61.   In case a student commits or contributes to misconduct relating to other academic
matters, the Dean of the faculty with which the student is affiliated shall determine the appropriate measures to be
taken, with provisions from Clause 60 applied mutatis mutandis.
Clause 62.   T he implementation under Clause 60 and Clause 6 1, in case the student's affiliated
faculty is not the faculty administering the course in which the misconduct occurred, shall be in accordance with the
university announcement and shall be overseen by a committee appointed as per that announcement.
Clause 63.   In the case where there exist reasonable grounds to consider the deduction of
behavioral points as outlined in Clause 60, the Dean or the relevant committee vested with the authority under
Clauses 60, Cla use 61, or Clause 62 , as applicable, may reduce the points deducted as considered expedient,
provided the reduction shall not be less than half of the points specified in Clause 60, and deductions must be
made in whole numbers.
Reasonable grounds under par agraph one are as follows:
(1)   T he student acknowledges the misconduct and takes steps to mitigate its negative impact.
(2)   The student confesses the misconduct to examiners, the Examination Board, the Dean, or the
relevant committee vested with the authority unde r Clause 60, Clause 61, or Clause 62, with the confession formally
documented in writing.
(3)   The student provides testimony or engages in actions that aid the proceedings ; or
(4)   Any other circumstances deemed equivalent by the Dean or by the relevant committee v ested
with the authority under Clause 60, Clause 61, or Clause 62, as applicable.
Clause 64.   Upon issuing disciplinary actions in accordance with Clause 60 or Clause 61 or based
on resolutions of the committee in accordance with Clause 62, the Dean of the faculty wit h which the student is
affiliated shall notify these actions to the Office of the Registrar for acknowledgment and undertake further steps .
Chapter 9
Suspension of Study
Clause 65.   In case a student is subjected to the suspension of study under applicable regulatio ns,
such suspension shall take effect from the semester immediately following the semester in which the misconduct
occur red , and t he duration of such suspension shall be consecutive and will be inclusive within the period of study .
During the suspension of study , students must pay the maintenance fee to maintain their student
status and shall be precluded from using university services, except healthcare - related student services .
In case a student commits misconduct in the semester wherein all program requi rements have been
fulfilled and is subsequently issued an order to suspend the study , the Administrative Board of the Faculty shall not
submit the student's name to the University Council for degree conferral or diploma conferral under Clause 72 until
the period of the suspension of study has lapsed .
Clause 66.   The suspended students must pay the maintenance fee to maintain their student
status for every semester in accordance with the university announcement . Otherwise, the student status shall be
terminated.
Chapt er 10
Termination and Reinstatement of Student Status
Clause 67.   A studen t status shall be terminated under the following circumstances:
(1)   Having fulfilled all program requirements and been conferred a degree in accordance with
Clause 69 ;
(2)   Having resign ed from the univ ersity, excepted the student has settled any outstanding fees to
the faculty or university in full ;
(3)   After the first 2 weeks o f the semester, f ailing to register for courses or to maintain student
status , with non - payment of tuition, late registration fees, or other academic - related fees (if applicable);
(4)   Obtaining a Cumulative Grade Point Average below 1.50 , following the classification of student
status ;
(5)   Remaining in a probationary status with a Cumulative Grade Point Average below 1.80 for two
consecutive semesters following the classification of student status ;
(6)   Remaining in a probationary status for 4 consecutive semesters following the classification of
student status without any transition out of the probationary status ;
(7)   After the period of study as outl ined in Clause 14 has been exhausted , having credits as
mandated by the program remain unfulfilled or obtaining a Cumulative Grade Point Average below 2.00 ;
(8)   Having received an order from the Dean effectuating the termination of student status under
Clause 60, Clause 61, or Clause 62 ;
(9)   Having v iolat ed university regulations or rules leading to an official order for the termination of
student status ;
(10) Death.
Clause 68.   Students whose status is terminated under Clause 67(3) may request for the
reinstatement of the student status within the semester of termination , contingent upon the endorsement of the
Administrative Board of the Faculty and the approval by the University President.
Chapter 11
Graduation
Section 1
Request for Receipt of Degree or Diploma
Clause 69.   Students sh all be eligible to submit a request for degree confer ral upon meeting the
following qualifications:
(1)   Being students in the final semester having registered for all courses required for the
completion of the program ;
(2)   Having met the requisite semester duratio n for program completion: f or a 4 - year program,
students must complete a minimum of 6 regular semesters ; for a 5 - year program, students must complete a
minimum of 8 regular semesters ; and for a 6 - year program, students must complete a minimum of 10 regular
semesters .
Clause 70.   Qualifications relating to diploma conferral shall be in accordance with the relevant
regulations of Chulalongkorn University.
Clause 71.   Students who meet the criteria outlined in Clause 69 and Clause 70 must declare their
intention to receive their degr ee or diploma, as prescribed by the announcement from the Office of Registrar. Failure
to do so may result in the imposition of a penalty fee in accordance with the university announcement and may be
excluded from the list of candidates presented to the Un iversity Council for degree or diploma confer ral for that
semester .
Section 2
Conferral of Degree or Diploma
Clause 72.   The Administrative Board of the Faculty with which the student is affiliated shall
consider students who have met the required qualifications and demonstrated good behavior suitable for being
conferred a degree or diploma and propose the ir names to the University Council for the formal approval of the
degree or diploma confe rral, provided the students have completed all examinations for the total c redits specified
by the program and have achieved a Cumulative Grade Point Average of no t less than 2.00.
The bestowal of Honors upon a Degree shall be in accordance with the relevant Chulalongkorn
University regulations.
Candidates endorsed by the Adminis trative Board of the Faculty as graduates by the final date of
the academic year as stipulated by the university and subsequently approved for graduation by the University
Council shall qualify to participate in the commencement of that academic year , prov ided there are no outstanding
tuition fees , fees, or other charges against them.
Section 3
Award of Distinction Medal
Clause 73.   Students   who are   eligible for a distinction medal must   meet   the following
qualifications :
(1)   Obtaining the First - Class Honors, and
(2)   Holding the highest Cumulative Grade Point Average in comparison to other graduates from the
same program within the same academic year
(3)   Not having any course exemptions as per Clause 25 .
The decision to award the distinction medal shall be executed at the completi on of each academic
year.
